display: I run a board-game café on Austin's east side (about 400 games, a playtest back room) and I'm designing a trading game about the 19th-century Fuzhou–London tea route, with a Kickstarter planned for March 2027.

signals.text: My tea-trade game has solid mechanics after about forty playtests, but the history feels thin. I need real human stories and real data behind it.
I'm looking for real Fuzhou-vs-London tea price series and clipper-race records. The one paper I found only gives averages.
I'm planning a Kickstarter for March 2027 and want to talk to people who have run board-game campaigns.
A US printer quoted $38 a copy for 2,000 units with custom wooden tea-chest tokens. That puts retail near $90, which is too high for an unknown designer.
I need a cheaper manufacturer, or a smarter split between custom and stock components, without losing the tea-chest feel.
I can't write my Kickstarter page. Every draft sentence feels wrong, and my pitch falls apart when a stranger asks what the game is about.
My back room sits empty on Monday afternoons and some other weekday afternoons, and I'd like someone to use it.
I want to fill weekday afternoons at the café without hiring another employee.
My playtesters have asked me to drop the Opium Wars material from the rulebook. I'm trying to work out how to treat a contested history respectfully.
I want playtesters from outside my regular Tuesday group, because nobody else has ever played the game.
I'm training for the Austin Half in February and could use running company or advice on knee care for early-morning runs.
Three years is a long time on one design. I want a hard deadline and someone who will hold me to the December prototype v1.0 date.

offers.text: A board-game café with about 400 games and a separate back room with acoustic panels, usable for playtests, meetups, workshops or small groups.
A weekly Tuesday-night playtest group of about fifteen regulars who give detailed, honest critique. I can host your unfinished design there.
Eleven years of high-school history teaching, so I can write clear rules, explain history simply and make cheap, effective handouts.
A complete paper prototype of a trading game (board, 90 cards, 60 wooden tokens) and about forty playtests of experience with its economy mechanics.
A 1,300-person board-game mailing list and a 400-member Discord that I can share relevant projects with.
Basic Kickstarter experience from helping two friends fund smaller games.
Afternoon space in the back room, most reliably on Mondays, at a cost or a trade that suits both sides.
I can run beginner chess or board-game sessions for kids, since I coach a school chess club.
Mornings before the café opens and Tuesday nights are my design time, so I can give feedback on other designers' prototypes.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I'm a historian of the China trade. I have price ledgers for Foochow and Mincing Lane from the 1860s and I'm looking for a way to get them in front of a wider audience.
catchers.can: Use the real numbers to rebuild Tea Road's price and risk mechanics, credit the source in the rulebook and put the data in front of my playtest group.
catchers.confirm: Does your material include actual per-season prices or voyage records, not just averages?

catchers.hypo: I make small-batch board games and have used a manufacturer in Asia or Europe. I can introduce you or share quotes for custom wooden pieces at 2,000 units.
catchers.can: Compare against my $38-per-copy quote and decide how many custom parts the campaign can afford.
catchers.confirm: Have you personally had a print run of at least 1,000 units with wooden components delivered?

catchers.hypo: I run a language exchange or hobby meetup in Austin and need a quiet, affordable room on weekday afternoons.
catchers.can: Offer the back room on Monday afternoons, which are empty today. It has acoustic panels, coffee and games, and the group needs no extra staff from me.
catchers.confirm: Does the group meet on weekday afternoons and run itself, with no need for staff to supervise?

catchers.hypo: I teach history or run a history club and want my students to play a game about real trade routes. Could we run a session?
catchers.can: Bring Tea Road to a classroom or club session as a playtest, adapt the rules for a lesson and trade feedback on the history.
catchers.confirm: Would your group of players be willing to give structured feedback on an unfinished game?

catchers.hypo: I'm a narrative designer or writer who loves historical fiction. I could write short merchant and captain stories for game cards.
catchers.can: Pair my mechanics with your stories and replace flat cards like 'Storm at the Cape, lose one chest' with ones that carry human stakes.
catchers.confirm: Do you write from documented historical sources rather than invented history?

catchers.hypo: I just launched my first board-game Kickstarter and want to compare notes on page copy, pricing tiers and shipping costs.
catchers.can: Share what I learned helping two friends fund games, and swap honest page-copy critique, which I'm stuck on for my own campaign.
catchers.confirm: Have you launched, or are you actively preparing, a tabletop crowdfunding campaign?

catchers.hypo: My designer friend needs honest playtesters and a place to test a prototype in Austin, since nobody local will tell them the truth.
catchers.can: Offer the Tuesday group and the back room for a playtest session. Marcus, my designer friend in Denver who has funded two games, could advise on the campaign.
catchers.confirm: Is your design at a stage where strangers can play a rough prototype with minimal explanation?

catchers.hypo: My child is twelve and loves chess but hates losing. Is there somewhere they can practice with other kids who are good at it?
catchers.can: Point them to my niece's school chess club, whose coach I help, where kids learn to lose and review their games.
catchers.confirm: Is your child between about ten and thirteen and willing to review their losses afterward?

catchers.hypo: I'm a sailing or maritime-history enthusiast. I know clipper-ship routes and how the Cape and monsoon seasons affected voyages.
catchers.can: Check the game's shipping and weather events against the real routes and seasons, and invite you to a playtest.
catchers.confirm: Can you speak to the actual sailing conditions on the China–London route, not just generic sea history?

forbids.text: I won't ship a game with invented history when real history is available.
The café stays open six days a week, so my design time is mornings and Tuesday nights only.
The first print run can't cost more than the Kickstarter is expected to raise.
I won't share customer-level information, such as names, orders or anything about the people who visit the café.
I'm not hiring a second employee to cover weekday afternoons.

projects.name: Tea Road
projects.text: A 2–5 player trading game on the Fuzhou–London tea route, 1860–1880. The mechanics are solid after about forty playtests. It needs stronger history, a viable manufacturing cost and a Kickstarter in March 2027.

projects.name: Café back-room weekday program
projects.text: Fill weekday afternoons in an acoustically treated back room with groups or events that need no extra staff.

policy.t1: When there's a real lead, I'll share specific design problems, the printer quote details, the Kickstarter plan, and which weekday afternoons the back room is free.
policy.t2: Once the match looks strong and I know who you are, I'll talk openly about my financial limits and my doubts about finishing the game.
policy.never: Anything about individual customers, and the personal details of my family and friends beyond a general description of their roles.
